title: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents, and Solutions

learn.hook: Stir sugar into nimbu pani and it vanishes. But taste it and the sweetness is everywhere! Where did the sugar go?
points: When a substance dissolves, it spreads evenly through another substance, forming a solution. A solution is a homogeneous mixture.
The substance that dissolves is the solute (sugar). The substance in which it dissolves is the solvent (water).
Mass is not lost when something dissolves: mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent.
Substances that dissolve in a solvent are soluble (salt, sugar in water). Those that do not are insoluble (sand, chalk powder in water).

Water dissolves so many substances that it is called the universal solvent. Other solvents exist too: nail-polish remover dissolves nail paint, and turpentine dissolves oil paint. Solutions can also hold gases, like carbon dioxide in soda water.

example.q: Think it through: Arjun dissolves 15 g of salt in 200 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
steps: Mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent

learn.reallife: The sea is a giant solution: salts are the solutes and water is the solvent. That is why the water tastes salty everywhere you swim.

quiz.q: In a solution of salt in water, which is the solvent?
quiz.explain: The solvent is the substance that does the dissolving, here water.
steps: The solvent is the substance that does the dissolving
Salt dissolves in water, so water is the solvent
Answer: Water
quiz.mistake: Mixes up solute and solvent

quiz.q: In sugar syrup, sugar is the:
quiz.explain: Sugar is the substance that dissolves, so it is the solute.
steps: The solute is the substance that dissolves
Sugar dissolves in water to make syrup, so sugar is the solute
Answer: Solute
quiz.mistake: Confuses the dissolving substance with the dissolved one

quiz.q: Neha dissolves 25 g of sugar in 100 g of water. What is the mass of the solution, in grams?
steps: Mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent
Answer: 125
quiz.explain: Dissolving does not destroy the sugar; its mass is added to the water's mass.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the dissolved solute has no mass

quiz.q: Why is water called the universal solvent?
options: It dissolves a very large number of substances
quiz.explain: Water dissolves more substances than most other liquids, though not all (sand and oil do not dissolve).
steps: Water dissolves more substances than most other liquids
It is not every substance (sand and oil do not dissolve), but a very large number
Answer: It dissolves a very large number of substances
quiz.mistake: Thinks water can dissolve absolutely everything

quiz.q: Which of these is insoluble in water?
quiz.explain: Sand settles at the bottom however much you stir.
steps: Salt, sugar and glucose dissolve in water
Sand settles at the bottom however much you stir, so sand is insoluble
Answer: Sand
quiz.mistake: Thinks stirring makes everything dissolve

quiz.q: A solution has the same composition throughout. So it is a:
quiz.explain: A solution is uniform everywhere, which makes it a homogeneous mixture.
steps: A solution is uniform everywhere
A mixture with the same composition throughout is a homogeneous mixture
Answer: Homogeneous mixture
quiz.mistake: Thinks a solution is a compound

quiz.q: In soda water, the gas carbon dioxide is the:
quiz.explain: Carbon dioxide is dissolved in water, so it is the solute. The fizz is the gas escaping.
steps: Carbon dioxide is dissolved in the water of soda
The dissolved substance is the solute; the fizz is the gas escaping
Answer: Solute
quiz.mistake: Thinks only solids can be solutes

quiz.q: Which solvent would you use to remove nail paint?
quiz.explain: Nail paint does not dissolve in water but dissolves in nail-polish remover, a different solvent.
steps: Nail paint does not dissolve in water
It dissolves in nail-polish remover, so that is the solvent to use
Answer: Nail-polish remover
quiz.mistake: Thinks water dissolves every substance

teach.ask: Gappu stirs sugar into his water: The sugar disappeared! Is it gone forever? What just happened?
teach.praise: The sugar, the solute, dissolved in water, the solvent, and spread evenly to make a solution. It is still there, just hiding sweetly!
teach.nudge: What do we call it when sugar spreads into water? What are the names of the sugar and the water?

revise.summary: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of a solute (what dissolves) in a solvent (what dissolves it). Mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent. Soluble substances dissolve; insoluble ones like sand do not. Water is the universal solvent; gases like CO₂ can be solutes.
remember: 15 g salt + 200 g water = 215 g solution
Water is the universal solvent, but sand and oil do not dissolve in it
In soda water, CO₂ is the solute
traps: 'Universal solvent' does not mean water dissolves everything
Mass is not lost when something dissolves
The solvent is the larger, dissolving part — not the solute

learn.hook: Keep adding sugar to a glass of cold water and a point comes when no more will dissolve. Warm it, and suddenly it can take in more. Why?
points: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that can dissolve in a fixed amount of solvent at a given temperature.
A solution in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature is saturated. If more can still dissolve, it is unsaturated.
For most solids, like sugar, solubility increases when the temperature rises. That is how sugar syrup for gulab jamun is made with hot water.
Gases are less soluble in warm water than in cold water. A warm soda bottle fizzes more when opened, and warm water holds less oxygen for fish.
Stirring and powdering make a solute dissolve faster, but they do not change how much can dissolve (the solubility).

example.q: Think it through: Sugar stops dissolving in a cup of water at room temperature. Riya warms the cup gently and the leftover sugar dissolves. What does this show?
steps: Sugar stopped dissolving, so the solution was saturated at room temperature.
After warming, more sugar dissolved.
So the solubility of sugar increased with temperature.
example.answer: The solubility of sugar increases with temperature; the warm solution can hold more sugar.

learn.reallife: Halwais make thick chashni for jalebis by dissolving a lot of sugar in hot water, far more than would dissolve in cold water.

quiz.q: What is a saturated solution?
options: One in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature
quiz.explain: A saturated solution holds the maximum solute it can at that temperature.
steps: A saturated solution holds the maximum solute it can
So no more solute can dissolve in it at that temperature
Answer: One in which no more solute can dissolve at that temperature
quiz.mistake: Thinks saturated just means strong-tasting

quiz.q: How can you dissolve more sugar in a saturated sugar solution?
quiz.explain: Raising the temperature increases the solubility of sugar.
steps: For sugar, solubility rises with temperature
So warming the solution lets more sugar dissolve
Answer: Warm it
quiz.mistake: Thinks cooling helps more solid dissolve

quiz.q: Why does a warm bottle of soda fizz more on opening than a cold one?
options: Gases are less soluble in warm water
The bottle is bigger when warm
quiz.explain: Warm water cannot hold as much carbon dioxide, so more gas escapes as fizz.
steps: Gases are less soluble in warm water
A warm soda holds less carbon dioxide, so more escapes as fizz
Answer: Gases are less soluble in warm water
quiz.mistake: Thinks gases behave like solids with temperature

quiz.q: Which change makes salt dissolve faster but does NOT change its solubility?
quiz.explain: Stirring speeds up dissolving but the maximum amount that can dissolve stays the same.
steps: Stirring speeds up dissolving
It does not change the maximum amount that can dissolve, unlike changing the temperature or solvent
Answer: Stirring
quiz.mistake: Confuses the rate of dissolving with solubility

quiz.q: Solubility is the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a fixed amount of solvent at a given:
quiz.explain: Solubility depends on temperature, so we must state it.
steps: Solubility changes with temperature
So it must be stated for a given temperature
Answer: Temperature
quiz.mistake: Does not know solubility depends on temperature

quiz.q: Why can water in a very warm pond be harder for fish?
options: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen
Fish cannot swim in warm water
quiz.explain: Oxygen is a gas, and gases are less soluble in warmer water.
steps: Oxygen is a gas, and gases are less soluble in warm water
So warm pond water holds less dissolved oxygen for fish
Answer: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen
quiz.mistake: Does not know gas solubility falls with temperature

quiz.q: Some sugar stays at the bottom of a glass of water after a lot of stirring. The solution above it is:
quiz.explain: If extra solute stays undissolved after stirring, the solution has reached its limit: it is saturated.
steps: Extra sugar stays undissolved after a lot of stirring
The solution has reached its limit, so it is saturated
Answer: Saturated
quiz.mistake: Does not recognise the sign of a saturated solution

quiz.q: Which dissolves fastest in water at the same temperature?
options: A jaggery block kept in a bag
quiz.explain: Powder has a much larger surface touching the water, so it dissolves faster.
steps: Powder has a much larger surface touching the water
So powdered jaggery dissolves fastest
Answer: Powdered jaggery
quiz.mistake: Does not link surface area with speed of dissolving

teach.ask: Gappu keeps adding sugar to his water: Why won't any more dissolve? Is my water broken?
teach.praise: My water is saturated: it reached its maximum! If I warm it, the solubility of sugar goes up and more dissolves. Not broken at all!
teach.nudge: Is there a limit to how much sugar water can hold? What happens if I warm it?

revise.summary: Solubility is the most solute that dissolves in a fixed amount of solvent at a given temperature. A saturated solution can take no more; an unsaturated one can. Most solids dissolve more when hot; gases less. Stirring and powdering speed dissolving but don't change solubility.
focus: Definition of solubility and saturated solutions
Effect of temperature on solids and gases
Speeding up dissolving versus changing solubility
remember: Saturated: no more solute dissolves at that temperature
Hot water dissolves more sugar; warm water holds less gas (oxygen, CO₂)
Stirring and powdering make dissolving faster only
traps: Gases dissolve less, not more, in warm water
Cooling a saturated sugar solution does not let more dissolve

learn.hook: Two glasses of sharbat look alike, but one tastes much sweeter. Science has a number for that sweetness: concentration!
points: Concentration tells us how much solute is present in a given amount of solution.
A dilute solution has a small amount of solute; a concentrated solution has a large amount. Adding more solvent makes a solution more dilute.
One way to express concentration is mass percentage: (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100.
Remember: mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent.
The right concentration matters. For example, a doctor or a packet's instructions tell exactly how much ORS powder to mix in how much water.

example.q: Think it through: 20 g of sugar is dissolved in 180 g of water. What is the concentration as a mass percentage?
steps: Mass of solution = 20 + 180 = 200 g
Concentration = (20 ÷ 200) × 100

learn.reallife: When you add water to a thick mango pulp to make juice, you are diluting it: the same pulp is spread through more water.

games.title: Least to most concentrated
games.prompt: Each glass has 100 g of solution. Order from most dilute to most concentrated.

quiz.q: 15 g of salt is dissolved in 135 g of water. What is the concentration, as a mass percentage?
steps: Mass of solution = 15 + 135 = 150 g
Answer: 10%
quiz.explain: Divide the solute's mass by the solution's mass (not the water's) and multiply by 100.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the mass of solvent instead of the mass of solution

quiz.q: A solution has 40 g of sugar in 200 g of solution. What is its concentration, as a mass percentage?
steps: Answer: 20%
quiz.explain: The total mass of solution is already given as 200 g.
quiz.mistake: Adds 40 to 200 even though 200 g is already the whole solution

quiz.q: How many grams of salt are in 300 g of a 5% salt solution?
steps: Answer: 15
quiz.explain: 5% means 5 g of solute in every 100 g of solution, so 300 g has 15 g.
quiz.mistake: Uses the percentage itself as the mass

quiz.q: What happens to the concentration of a sugar solution when more water is added?
quiz.explain: The same sugar is spread through more solution, so it becomes more dilute.
steps: The same sugar is spread through more solution
So the solution becomes more dilute: its concentration decreases
Answer: It decreases
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding solvent increases concentration

quiz.q: A dilute solution has:
options: A small amount of solute in it
quiz.explain: Dilute means relatively little solute for the amount of solution.
steps: Dilute means relatively little solute
for the amount of solution, so a dilute solution has a small amount of solute
Answer: A small amount of solute in it
quiz.mistake: Mixes up dilute and concentrated

quiz.q: Glass A has 10 g of sugar in 100 g of solution. Glass B has 10 g of sugar in 200 g of solution. Which is more concentrated?
quiz.explain: A is 10% while B is 5%. The same sugar in less solution means higher concentration.
steps: 10 g of sugar in 100 g of solution: (10 ÷ 100) × 100 = 10%
10 g of sugar in 200 g of solution: (10 ÷ 200) × 100 = 5%
10% is more than 5%, so the glass with 100 g of solution is more concentrated
Answer: Glass A
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal solute mass means equal concentration

quiz.q: 8 g of glucose is dissolved in 92 g of water. What is the mass of the solution, in grams?
quiz.explain: Mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent = 8 + 92 = 100 g.
steps: Given: solute = 8 g glucose, solvent = 92 g water
Mass of solution = mass of solute + mass of solvent
Answer: 100
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the solute's mass

quiz.q: Why should ORS be made exactly as the instructions say?
options: The right concentration of salts and sugar is needed for it to work safely
quiz.explain: Too strong or too weak a solution may not help the body properly, so the concentration matters.
steps: ORS works only at the right concentration
Too strong or too weak may not help the body properly, so follow the instructions exactly
Answer: The right concentration of salts and sugar is needed for it to work safely
quiz.mistake: Thinks concentration does not matter in real life

teach.ask: Gappu makes two cups of sharbat: Why is one so much sweeter? How can I say which is stronger?
teach.praise: Concentration tells how much solute is in the solution. More sugar in the same amount of sharbat means more concentrated!
teach.nudge: What tells us how strong a solution is? What should we compare in the two cups?

revise.summary: Concentration is how much solute is in a given amount of solution. Dilute solutions have little solute and concentrated ones a lot; adding solvent dilutes. Mass percentage = (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100, where solution = solute + solvent. Correct concentration matters, as in ORS.
remember: Mass % = (mass of solute ÷ mass of solution) × 100
20 g sugar + 180 g water = 200 g solution → 10%
traps: Divide by the mass of solution, not the mass of solvent
More powder in ORS is not better
